spec_note_claims.only_v0_6_0_wrote_path: FALSE. git grep over the tags: v0.1.0 through v0.5.0 all have cmd/relay/relay.go handleContextGet writing closeMeta {"path": filePath} under schemaHTTPBody (index 2). v0.2.0 through v0.5.0 name https://github.com/buildwarden/buildwarden/schemas/v1/http-body.json at index 2 (cmd/relay/ledger.go:65), and their schemas/v1/http-body.json already has additionalProperties: false; v0.1.0 named schemas/http-body.json, which had no published schema file. b716d9e (2026-09-24) only widened the key to the build script, and 4ea4f50 to the bootstrap config. So v0.2.0-v0.5.0 ledgers carry path on every build-context-file close; v0.6.0 adds the build-script and bootstrap closes.
spec_note_claims.readers_ignore_it: true. No Go code outside tests reads a "path" key from ledger metadata; cmd/warden inspect metaSummary (cmd/warden/inspect_impl.go:636-639) reads only method, url, name, reference. inspect_env.go's Path json tag is environment metadata, not http-body.
spec_note_claims.metadata_outside_signature: true. relay/ledger.go loop() signs type, prev_sig, open_sig (non-OPEN), payload size and hash block only; schema index and CBOR metadata are appended after the signature. specs/build-ledger/v1.md:15 says metadata is not part of signatures.
spec_note_claims.path_duplicates_open_url: true for every release: path is req.URL.Path with the leading slash trimmed (build-script, bootstrap, src/main.c against http://artifacts/build-script, http://artifacts/bootstrap, http://cwd/src/main.c).

findings.finding: The Known producer deviation note understates the deviation. It says ledgers written by the v0.6.0 relay, and unreleased builds from b716d9e onward, carry path. The release history says otherwise: v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.4.0 and v0.5.0 (cmd/relay/relay.go handleContextGet, line 536-537 in each tag) also write {"path": <file>} on every build-context-file close under index 2, and their header names the same schemas/v1/http-body.json $id with additionalProperties: false. b716d9e only extended the key to the build script (and 4ea4f50 to the bootstrap config). A third-party reader of this long-lived spec would take v0.2.0-v0.5.0 ledgers to conform strictly, and they do not. The same false premise is in the design (docs/design/http-body-path-drift.md:39-42 'v0.5.0 had no such field; v0.6.0 ... is the only release whose ledgers carry it', and D3 at :128, plan step 4 at :300-301) and in the a1/a2 question text Jeff confirmed. The decision does not move: option C's own argument (old ledgers stay non-conforming to the v1 schema they name) gets stronger, and readers-ignore-it and metadata-unsigned stay true.
findings.suggestion: wf-implement: in a new commit (no amend, no force-push) rewrite the note to say ledgers from v0.2.0 through v0.6.0 carry a path text field on the http-body close of each build-context file, and v0.6.0 (from b716d9e and 4ea4f50) also on the build-script and bootstrap closes; keep 'duplicates the open record's url', 'readers ignore it' and 'current relays write {"status": 200}'. Commit it alone with a fresh trailer, e.g. 'Tier1-Allow: RELAY-05 specs/metadata-http-body/v1.md: correct the releases the deviation note names; schema unchanged (http-body-path-drift)'. Correct the design's History paragraph (:39-42), D3 (:128) and plan step 4 (:300-301) to the same facts in the same or a separate commit, and say in the PR body that a1/a2 were confirmed on the 'v0.6.0 only' premise, which was wrong but does not change the choice. Not back-to-design.

findings.finding: The drift guard is real (verified red on the old producer and on an injected key in artifact metadata) but covers only what the end-to-end scenario reaches: records under http-open, http-headers, http-body (served inputs only) and artifact. The other http-body producers, the request-body checkpoint {} (relay/relay.go:527), the bodiless upstream response close {"status"} (relay.go:578) and the streamed response close (relay.go:799), and redacted and environment metadata, are never written in that scenario, so a future extra key there passes. The design says this honestly ('every metadata producer the scenario reaches'); the gap is in what the guard promises beyond this bug.
findings.suggestion: Optional follow-up, not for this PR: drive one proxied upstream GET and one request-body POST through the scenario (or a second scenario against an httptest upstream) so every http-body producer is checked, or state the covered schema indices in the test's doc comment.

findings.finding: TestRelayCollectorEndToEnd now only calls runEndToEndScenario, and TestLedgerMetadataConformsToSpecs runs the same whole scenario again (about 2 s each, a relay plus a real collector), so the relay package pays for the scenario twice; the conformance test's first call already performs every assertion TestRelayCollectorEndToEnd makes.
findings.suggestion: Optional: run the scenario once and make the conformance check a subtest of TestRelayCollectorEndToEnd (t.Run("metadata conforms to specs", ...)) over the returned directory, or mark the two tests t.Parallel() if the scenario holds no shared state.
